_readme: The assistant's stubbed answer source. `qa` holds the suggested questions per context (print, fix, m1, planA, planB). kind: answer | notin | judge | safety | off. `keywords` let the stub match typed questions. The safety message is fixed and never generated.
safety: Stop the printer if it’s safe to, and tell staff right now.
safetyFoot: Fixed safety message · always the same · not written by AI
notin: I don’t have that in TechCentral’s guide, so I don’t want to guess. Staff at the desk can help — they’re [[desk direction, two or three words|to your left]].
off: I can only help with printing and 3D printing here. For anything else, staff can point you the right way.
judgeGeneric: I can point you to the rules, but whether that’s OK is a staff call. Show them at the desk.

foots.notin: The assistant only answers from TechCentral’s guide.
foots.judge: The assistant can quote rules but never approves a print or rules on policy.
foots.off: This kiosk covers printing and 3D printing only.

print.a: Black and white is [[B&W price per page|10¢]] a page and color is [[color price per page|25¢]] a page. You pay at the release station when you print.

print.q: What if my file won’t open?
print.a: Open [[word processor|Microsoft Word]] first, then use File → Open to find your file. If it still won’t open, staff can take a look.
print.based: Step: open your file and print

print.q: Can I renew my books here?

fix.q: How long does my job wait?
fix.a: Jobs wait at the release station for [[how long jobs are held|2 hours]]. After that they’re cleared, and you’ll need to print again.
fix.based: Fix: job isn’t at the release station

fix.q: Can I get a refund for a misprint?
fix.a: Here’s the rule: “[[misprint refund policy|Staff can credit pages a printer jam ruined.]]” Whether your print qualifies is a staff call. Show them the print at the desk.

m1.q: What does “checked out on the printers” mean?
m1.a: It means staff have watched you run a print and signed you off [[the actual qualification rule|— the 3D printing orientation plus one supervised print]]. Until then, staff print for you.

m1.q: Can I run it myself today?
m1.a: Here’s the rule: “[[qualification rule|You need the 3D printing orientation and one supervised print.]]” Whether you can run it yourself is a staff call. Ask at the desk.

m1.q: Can I print a cosplay prop?
m1.a: Here’s the rule: “[[prohibited items policy|No weapons or weapon parts, and no replicas that could be mistaken for the real thing.]]” Whether your print fits is a staff call. Show them your file at the desk.

planA.a: Usually about [[turnaround|3 to 5 days]]. If you haven’t heard from us by then, ask at the desk.
planA.based: Step 4: wait, then pick it up

planA.a: We accept [[accepted file types|.STL, .OBJ, and .3MF files]]. Most free model sites let you download one of these.
Here’s the rule: “[[size and time limits|Up to 5 × 5 × 5 inches, and under 6 hours to print.]]” Whether your model fits is a staff call. Show them your file at the desk.

planA.q: Can you print my design in metal?

planB.q: How do I book a printer?
planB.a: [[booking method|Book at cpl.org/tc/book or at the desk]]. Bookings last [[booking length|up to 3 hours]].

planB.q: The printer is making a grinding noise
Can I leave while it prints?
planB.a: No. [[unattended printing policy|Staff stop prints left alone.]] If you need to step away, tell staff first.

planB.q: Can I use my own filament?
planB.a: Here’s the rule: “[[materials policy|Only library filament is used on library printers.]]” Whether your filament can be used is a staff call. Ask at the desk.
